title: "School reports at matched disclosure"
subtitle: "5.9 · the public twelve-school CDE example"
description: "Expected-error distribution of the three-grade reports that state 48 pairs."
---

The tertiles state as many comparisons as any report with three grades for these twelve schools.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/cde-one-disclosure.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["cde-one-disclosure"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

The figure gives the expected error range for each number of stated pairs. At the maximum of 48 pairs,
the histogram compares the tertiles with every other report stating that many. The lower convex boundary
also considers choosing among complete reports at random.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **At the tertiles’ disclosure** shows all 34,650 reports at N = 48. The tertiles have the fewest expected errors, with E = 1.829. The next report has E = 1.909.
- **Between feasible disclosures** selects N = 46. No single report in this family states exactly 46 pairs, while the lower hull reaches H = .4551 by a mixture with weight .500 on the more-disclosing report.
- **A lower mixture** selects N = 30. The hull value is .005174, using weight .167 on the more-disclosing endpoint.
- **Other cuts, full range** places cuts at 1 and 2. The selected report states 21 pairs and expects 1.116 wrong directions; the enlarged axis shows the complete ranges at every disclosure.

Only three groups of four can reach 48 stated pairs. A randomized rule that averages 48 stated pairs must choose only reports at that maximum. The tertiles already have the fewest expected errors among those reports, so randomization cannot improve on them at 48.

The mixture weight is the probability of choosing the report that states more pairs. The histogram and the table available by keyboard give the full error distribution. A shorter table lists the five reports with the fewest expected errors.

Data: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26, as adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (`pr_case_cde`). This deliberately spread twelve-school teaching subset is conditional on a statewide prior fitted to 5,834 eligible schools; prior-estimation uncertainty is not propagated. CDE source conditions apply (<https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp>); the data are not relicensed and are provided as is without warranty. No CDE endorsement is implied.

The error distribution applies to comparisons of chronic absence within this subset. A shared grade leaves a comparison unstated. California's Dashboard colors use separate rules, and the distribution provides no basis for estimating school quality, causal effects, statewide optimality, or calibration.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## In postrank

This call uses the supplied posterior to evaluate the fixed tertiles at τ .20.

```r
library(postrank)
g <- pr_case_cde$reference$actions$observed_rate_tertiles
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_case_cde$input, weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = .2)[c("N", "E", "primary_risk")]
```
:::
